references.topic: Design-bid-build family: owner–architect, owner–contractor (stipulated sum), general conditions. All three are on NCARB's ARE list.
Owner–construction manager as constructor; cost of the work plus a fee with a GMP. On NCARB's ARE list.
Design-build: owner–design-builder; design-builder–architect. On NCARB's ARE list.
Integrated project delivery (transitional) agreements. On NCARB's ARE list.
Architect–consultant agreement. On NCARB's ARE list.
Instructions to Bidders. On NCARB's ARE list.
Other members of the owner–architect and delivery-method families referenced in the note.
references.confidenceNote: Not on NCARB's ARE list; document numbers and edition years from my knowledge. Confirm on aiacontracts.com.

questions.stem:
A regional hospital system is planning a 180-bed patient tower. After a year of planning, its board has set these goals for the project:

- Contractor input on cost and constructability during design
- A guaranteed maximum price before construction documents are complete, to secure bond financing
- Early site work and foundations while design continues
- A direct contract with its own architect, who will represent the system's interests

Which delivery method best meets these goals?

options.explanation: DBB prices the work only after documents are complete, with no early contractor input.
Correct. A CMc provides preconstruction input, a GMP before CDs are complete, and phased early starts, while the owner contracts directly with the architect.
A CM adviser provides input but carries no cost risk and offers no GMP.
Design-build puts the architect under the design-builder, so the owner loses a direct contract with its architect.

questions.explanation: Early cost input + GMP + fast-track + direct owner–architect contract → CMc (A133 with B133).

questions.stem:
A distribution company hires a design-build firm under AIA A141-2014 to deliver a 400,000 sf warehouse. The design-builder engages an architect under AIA B143-2014. Midway through design, the company's facilities manager calls the architect directly and asks for changes to the loading-dock layout, saying the architect 'works for the project.' The architect's agreement addresses communications with the owner, and the design-builder's project executive is away for two weeks.

To whom does the architect owe its contractual obligations?

options.explanation: The company contracts with the design-builder (A141). The architect has no direct agreement with it.
Correct. B143 is the agreement between the design-builder and the architect, so change requests should go through the design-builder.
Contractual duties run only to the party the architect contracts with.
Code-compliance duties to the public exist, but they aren't the contractual relationship.

questions.explanation: In design-build, the architect is often the design-builder's consultant, not the owner's independent agent.

questions.stem:
A city charter requires construction contracts to be awarded to the lowest responsive, responsible bidder. For a new public works yard, the city wants the architect to serve as its independent representative during construction. The city attorney asks the architect which AIA documents to use. The public works director has managed several design-bid-build projects and wants construction pricing that's easy to defend at council meetings. The yard includes vehicle maintenance bays and fuel storage.

Which AIA documents fit this project?

options.explanation: Correct. The standard owner–architect agreement for design-bid-build.
Correct. The owner–contractor stipulated-sum agreement, suited to low-bid award.
Correct. Instructions to Bidders for the competitive bid process.
A133 is for a construction manager as constructor with a GMP, not low-bid award.
B143 is the design-builder–architect agreement.
A195 is for integrated project delivery.

questions.explanation: Competitive low bid + independent architect → design-bid-build (B101, A101/A201, A701).

questions.stem:
A county is planning a justice center and will hire a construction manager to advise on cost, schedule and constructability during design. The county wants to bid the work in several trade packages and hold the trade contracts itself, keeping all construction cost risk with the trade contractors. The architect will be hired under a separate agreement. The county's board approved the project after two years of planning, and the construction budget is $95 million.

Which arrangement fits the county's goals?

options.explanation: Correct. A CMa advises the owner without contracting for construction or taking cost risk.
A CMc holds the trade contracts and takes cost risk above its GMP.
The design-builder takes responsibility for both design and construction cost.

options.text: General contractor with a stipulated sum
options.explanation: The general contractor takes cost risk on its contract price.

questions.explanation: CMa = adviser, no cost risk. CMc = constructor, GMP risk.

questions.stem:
An owner's attorney revises a B101-2017 for a 200-unit apartment project to require weekly site visits during the 16-month construction period, instead of the twice-monthly visits in the architect's proposal. The attorney makes no change to the A201-2017 general conditions or to the architect's compensation, and the owner signs the revised agreement. The architect's fee assumed about 32 site visits. Weekly visits would require about 69.

What is the most significant consequence for the architect?

options.explanation: Correct. Doubling the visits needs a matching fee, and the A201 provisions on the architect's construction-phase role should be coordinated.

options.text: Responsibility for construction means and methods
options.explanation: More frequent visits don't by themselves transfer means and methods, which stay with the contractor.

options.text: Automatic updating of the A201 to match
options.explanation: Each document has to be modified deliberately. Nothing updates automatically.

options.text: No consequence, since visits are discretionary
options.explanation: The number of visits defines the architect's services and fee.

questions.explanation: When modifying contracts, check the scope and fee impact and coordination across the document family.

questions.stem:
An owner planning a technically complex research facility is considering integrated project delivery after hearing about it at a conference. Before deciding, the owner's board asks the architect to explain how IPD differs from the owner's usual design-bid-build approach. The facility will house specialized laboratories with complex mechanical systems, and the owner's last lab building suffered extensive change orders. The owner's construction director favors IPD, while its procurement office is skeptical.

Which characteristics generally describe IPD?

options.explanation: Correct. Designers, constructors and key trades join early.
Correct. Compensation is tied to shared outcomes.

options.text: Heavy reliance on shared BIM and collaboration tools
options.explanation: Correct. IPD typically depends on integrated digital workflows.

options.text: Minimal owner involvement after contract execution
options.explanation: IPD requires an engaged owner throughout.

options.text: Competitive low-bid selection of the constructor
options.explanation: IPD teams are selected for collaboration and qualifications.

options.text: The architect as the owner's agent against the contractor
options.explanation: IPD aligns the parties as collaborators rather than adversaries.

questions.explanation: IPD = early involvement, shared risk and reward, collaboration, an engaged owner.

questions.stem:
A restaurant franchise owner wants a new location open before peak season, eleven months away. The owner has no in-house design or construction staff and doesn't want to manage separate contracts with a designer and a builder. The prototype design is well developed, and the owner cares more about schedule certainty than fine design control. Two contractors in the region have built the prototype before, and local permitting typically takes about two months.

Which owner priorities favor design-build?

options.explanation: Correct. Design-build puts design and construction under one contract.

options.text: Overlapping design and construction for speed
options.explanation: Correct. Design-build readily supports fast-track overlap.

options.text: Limited capacity to manage separate contracts
options.explanation: Correct. One contract suits an owner without in-house project staff.

options.text: Detailed owner control over design decisions
options.explanation: An independent owner's architect (DBB or bridging) gives more design control.

options.text: Independent oversight of the contractor's work
options.explanation: In design-build, the designer is part of the contractor's team.
Competitive bidding on complete documents is design-bid-build.

questions.explanation: Design-build trades owner control and independent oversight for speed and single-source responsibility.

questions.stem:
An architect has signed a B101-2017 agreement for a K-12 school and is now engaging a structural engineer and an MEP engineer. The architect wants the consultants' obligations, insurance and schedules to line up with the prime agreement, and the school district asks which standard form will be used. The structural engineer has worked with the firm for ten years without a written agreement, and the MEP engineer is new to the firm. The district requires every consultant to carry professional liability insurance.

Which AIA document is intended for these agreements?

options.explanation: Correct. C401 is the architect–consultant agreement and aligns consultants' obligations with the prime agreement.
B101 is the owner–architect agreement.
C106 is a digital data licensing agreement.
A201 is the general conditions of the construction contract.

questions.stem:
Under a construction manager as constructor agreement, an owner wants the guaranteed maximum price set at 50% design development so it can close construction financing three months earlier. The construction manager is willing but says it will carry allowances and a design contingency. The owner asks the architect whether there's any downside. The project is a 300,000 sf corporate headquarters on an aggressive schedule. Design development drawings are about half complete, and fit-out requirements for two floors are still undefined.

Which risk should the architect explain?

options.text: Scope disputes over the incomplete documents
options.explanation: Correct. An early GMP rests on assumptions. Later design development may be disputed as a change or absorbed by contingency.

options.text: Architect liability for any amount over the GMP
options.explanation: The construction manager, not the architect, commits to the GMP.

options.text: Loss of the CM's preconstruction role
options.explanation: Preconstruction services continue after the GMP is set.

options.text: Exclusion of contingencies from the GMP
options.explanation: Early GMPs typically include contingencies for design completion.

questions.explanation: Early GMPs speed cost commitment but depend on clearly written assumptions and allowances.

questions.stem:
A general contractor is preparing a bid for a stipulated-sum project under AIA A101-2017 and A201-2017. The bid package includes instructions to bidders, a bid form, the drawings and specifications, and two addenda. The contractor's estimator asks which documents will become part of the contract if the firm wins the work. The project is a 50,000 sf office building with a stipulated sum of about $14 million.

Which items will be Contract Documents, unless the agreement enumerates otherwise?

options.explanation: Correct. The Agreement is a Contract Document.
Correct. The Conditions of the Contract are Contract Documents.
Correct. Drawings and specifications are Contract Documents.
Correct. Addenda issued before execution become part of the Contract Documents.
Bidding requirements aren't Contract Documents unless specifically enumerated.
The bid isn't a Contract Document unless the agreement specifically enumerates it.

questions.explanation: Contract Documents = agreement, conditions, drawings, specifications, addenda issued before execution, other listed documents, and modifications (A201-2017 §1.1.1).
questions.confidenceNote: Summarizes A201-2017 §1.1.1 as I understand it; confirm against your copy.

questions.stem:
A construction manager as constructor completes a project under a GMP agreement. The agreement provides that savings below the GMP are shared 60% to the owner and 40% to the construction manager. At final accounting: The project was a 120,000 sf office building finished two months early. The owner's accountant has reviewed the CM's cost records and agrees with the final figures.

- Guaranteed maximum price: $8,400,000
- Final cost of the work plus the CM's fee: $7,950,000

How much of the savings does the construction manager receive?

options.explanation: Correct. Savings of $450,000 × 40% = $180,000.
That's the owner's 60% share.
That's the total savings, before the split.
This applies 40% to the final cost instead of to the savings.

flashcards.back: A133-2019 (with GMP) or A134 (without); owner–architect B133.

flashcards.confidenceNote: Not on NCARB's ARE list; confirm edition years.

flashcards.front: IPD documents on the ARE list

flashcards.back: CMa = adviser, no cost risk. CMc = constructor with a GMP, holds the trade contracts.

flashcards.front: Design-build: whose agent is the architect?
flashcards.back: Usually the design-builder's (under B143), not the owner's.
Overlapping design and construction via sequential packages. A schedule strategy, not a delivery method.
The owner's architect prepares preliminary design and performance criteria; a design-builder completes and builds it.
Longest schedule; cost unknown until bids; no early contractor input.
It's based on incomplete documents, which leads to disputes over scope, allowances and contingency.
Stipulated sum; cost plus fee with GMP; cost plus fee without GMP; unit price.
Check the risk shift, insurability, the fee and scope impact, and coordination with the related documents (e.g., B101 ↔ A201).
